note: Every compound and blend in the Library, with the status, evidence grade and goals of the ones that have a fact sheet. Written by scripts/build_library.mjs for Miracle AI (miraclehealth.us/ai).

items.name: AOD-9604
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A lab-made fragment of human growth hormone taken for fat loss; it was developed as an obesity drug, but its main weight-loss trial failed and it is not approved.

items.name: Anastrozole
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription pill that blocks estrogen production, approved to treat hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause; it has also been studied off-label in men with low testosterone.

items.name: Armodafinil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for sleep disorders; Schedule IV
items.summary: The R-form of modafinil: a prescription wakefulness drug for sleep disorders, used off-label for focus with little direct evidence in healthy people.

items.name: Ashwagandha
items.status_label: Dietary supplement (banned in Denmark)
items.summary: An Ayurvedic herb (Withania somnifera) whose root extracts are taken mainly to ease stress and anxiety and to improve sleep.

items.name: BPC-157
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding not yet allowed
items.summary: A 15-amino-acid fragment of a protein first found in human stomach juice, taken for tendon, muscle and gut healing based mostly on rodent studies.

items.name: Berberine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A plant compound from goldenseal, barberry and Oregon grape, taken mainly to lower blood sugar and for weight loss.

items.name: Bronchogen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A four-amino-acid peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the lungs and airways; evidence so far is limited to cell and rat studies.

items.name: CJC-1295 no DAC (Mod GRF 1-29)
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A modified copy of the hormone that triggers growth hormone release, sold as a research chemical to raise growth hormone; evidence comes only from related peptides.

items.name: CJC-1295 with DAC
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A long-acting, lab-made version of the hormone that triggers growth hormone release, taken to raise growth hormone and IGF-1; human data come from short studies in healthy adults.

items.name: Cabergoline
items.status_label: FDA-approved for high prolactin (hyperprolactinemia)
items.summary: A prescription pill that lowers high prolactin by acting like dopamine on the pituitary; approved for hyperprolactinemia, including prolactin-making pituitary tumors.

items.name: Cagrilintide
items.status_label: Investigational; CagriSema under FDA review
items.summary: An experimental long-acting version of the hormone amylin, tested for weight loss alone and with semaglutide (as CagriSema); it is not FDA-approved.

items.name: Canagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, heart and kidney risk
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Invokana, that lowers blood sugar and heart and kidney risks in type 2 diabetes; anti-aging interest rests on a mouse study.

items.name: Cerebrolysin
items.status_label: Not approved in the US; prescription drug abroad
items.summary: A mixture of small peptides from pig brain, prescribed abroad for stroke and dementia and taken for focus and memory; not approved in the US, with weak supporting evidence.

items.name: Clomiphene
items.status_label: FDA-approved for ovulation induction; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription fertility pill that triggers ovulation in women who don't ovulate regularly; it is also used off-label in men to raise their own testosterone.

items.name: CoQ10
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A substance the body makes that helps cells produce energy, taken for heart health, statin-related muscle aches, migraine and energy.

items.name: Collagen peptides
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; not FDA-evaluated for these uses
items.summary: Collagen broken down into small protein fragments, taken by mouth mainly to improve skin hydration, elasticity and wrinkles, and sometimes for joint symptoms.

items.name: Creatine monohydrate
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A compound the body makes and gets from animal foods, taken as a supplement to add strength and power for short, intense exercise.

items.name: Crystagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A three-amino-acid peptide (Glu-Asp-Pro) from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted to support immunity in older people; evidence is mainly the developers' own small studies.

items.name: Curcumin
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; also a common spice
items.summary: The main yellow compound in turmeric, taken mostly for joint pain and inflammation; evidence is preliminary, and turmeric supplements have been linked to rare liver injury.

items.name: DHEA
items.status_label: Supplement; prescription vaginal form approved
items.summary: A hormone made by the adrenal glands that the body converts to testosterone and estrogen; sold as a supplement for libido, well-being and aging, with weak evidence.

items.name: DSIP
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A nine-amino-acid peptide, also called emideltide, first found in rabbit brain blood and taken in hopes of better sleep; evidence that it works is weak.

items.name: Dapagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for kidney disease, heart failure, diabetes
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Farxiga, that makes the kidneys pass extra sugar into the urine; it treats type 2 diabetes and lowers kidney and heart failure risks.

items.name: Dihexa
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: A lab-made compound based on the peptide angiotensin IV, used to try to boost memory; it improved learning in rodents, and FDA found no human data on it.

items.name: Dulaglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes and heart-risk reduction
items.summary: A prescription injection, sold as Trulicity, that activates GLP-1 receptors to lower blood sugar in type 2 diabetes and reduce the risk of heart attack and stroke.

items.name: Dutasteride
items.status_label: FDA-approved for enlarged prostate; off-label for hair
items.summary: A prescription capsule that blocks DHT production, approved in the US for an enlarged prostate; it is used off-label for male pattern hair loss.

items.name: Empagliflozin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, heart failure and kidney disease
items.summary: A prescription pill, sold as Jardiance, that makes the kidneys pass extra sugar into the urine; it treats type 2 diabetes and lowers heart failure and kidney risks.

items.name: Enclomiphene
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: One of the two forms in the fertility drug clomiphene, studied as a pill to raise men's own testosterone; it is not approved in the US or Europe.

items.name: Epitalon
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding status under FDA review
items.summary: A lab-made four-amino-acid peptide from Russian aging research, taken in hopes of slowing aging and restoring melatonin rhythms; human evidence is very thin.

items.name: Estradiol
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription hormone
items.summary: The body's most potent estrogen, prescribed mainly to relieve menopausal hot flashes and vaginal symptoms and to prevent bone loss after menopause.

items.name: Exemestane
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription pill that irreversibly blocks aromatase, the enzyme that makes estrogen, approved for hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause; studies in men are few and brief.

items.name: Exenatide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes; brands discontinued
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 medicine, first approved as Byetta in 2005, that lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes; the brand-name versions were discontinued in the US in 2024.

items.name: FSH
items.status_label: FDA-approved biologics for female and male infertility
items.summary: A prescription fertility hormone injection, made by recombinant DNA technology, approved for ovulation induction and IVF in women and, with hCG, to start sperm production in men.

items.name: Finasteride
items.status_label: FDA-approved for hair loss and enlarged prostate
items.summary: A prescription pill that blocks the conversion of testosterone to DHT, approved for male pattern hair loss and enlarged prostate; sexual and mood side effects are a known concern.

items.name: Follistatin 344
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A natural protein that blocks myostatin, a brake on muscle growth; taken to build muscle, it has been tested in people as a gene therapy for muscle diseases.

items.name: GHK-Cu
items.status_label: Non-injectable compounding allowed; injectable under review
items.summary: A small copper-binding peptide found naturally in human blood, used in skin creams and injected for skin, hair and healing, based mostly on small cosmetic and animal studies.

items.name: GHRP-2
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: A lab-made peptide that releases growth hormone and increases appetite; used in Japan as a diagnostic test and sold elsewhere as a research chemical.

items.name: GHRP-6
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: An early lab-made peptide that releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor, sold as a research chemical to raise growth hormone; human studies are small and short.

items.name: Glutathione
items.status_label: Compoundable while FDA evaluates; also a supplement
items.summary: An antioxidant the body makes, taken by mouth or IV for liver health, detox and skin lightening; human studies are small and IV use has caused serious reactions.

items.name: Glycine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: An amino acid taken mainly to improve sleep; the evidence is three small, very short trials in healthy adults.

items.name: Gonadorelin
items.status_label: No US product; compounding appears to be allowed
items.summary: A lab-made copy of the brain hormone GnRH, which tells the pituitary to release LH and FSH; men take it to support testicular function, with little evidence.

items.name: HGH Fragment 176-191
items.status_label: Not approved; sold as a research chemical
items.summary: A lab-made piece of the tail end of human growth hormone, sold as a research chemical for fat loss; the evidence comes from animal studies of a related peptide.

items.name: Hexarelin
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A lab-made relative of GHRP-6 that releases growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor, sold as a research chemical; human data come from a few small studies.

items.name: Humanin
items.status_label: Not approved; not nominated for compounding
items.summary: A small peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA that protects cells in lab and animal studies; levels fall with age, but it is untested as a treatment in people.

items.name: IGF-1 DES
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A shortened, more potent form of IGF-1 missing its first three amino acids, sold as a research chemical for muscle growth; evidence is limited to lab studies.

items.name: IGF-1 LR3
items.status_label: Not approved; not on FDA's compounding lists
items.summary: A lab-made, more potent form of IGF-1 that escapes the body's IGF-1 binding proteins, sold as a research chemical for muscle growth; evidence is limited to lab studies.

items.name: Ipamorelin
items.status_label: Not approved; on FDA's safety-risk list (503B)
items.summary: A small lab-made peptide taken to raise growth hormone through the ghrelin receptor; its only treatment trial, for bowel recovery after surgery, missed its main goal.

items.name: Iron
items.status_label: Dietary supplement (child-poisoning warning)
items.summary: An essential mineral needed to make hemoglobin, taken to prevent or treat iron deficiency and the anemia and fatigue it can cause.

items.name: KPV
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA compounding decision pending
items.summary: A three-amino-acid fragment of the hormone alpha-MSH, used for gut and skin inflammation on the strength of cell and animal studies; never tested in people.

items.name: Kisspeptin-10
items.status_label: FDA Category 2: pharmacies may not compound it
items.summary: The smallest fully active fragment of kisspeptin, a natural hormone that switches on the reproductive hormone chain; taken to raise testosterone and for sexual health.

items.name: L-theanine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; GRAS food ingredient
items.summary: An amino acid from tea leaves, taken to feel calm without drowsiness, ease stress, and improve sleep quality and focus.

items.name: LL-37
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: The body's own germ-fighting and inflammation-steering peptide, made by immune and skin cells, taken for immune support and wound healing; human evidence is limited to leg-ulcer trials.

items.name: Letrozole
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; other uses off-label
items.summary: A prescription pill that blocks estrogen production, approved for hormone-sensitive breast cancer after menopause; it is also used off-label to trigger ovulation and in men with low testosterone.

items.name: Leuprolide
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription drug
items.summary: A prescription hormone-blocking injection that switches off the body's sex-hormone production, used for prostate cancer, endometriosis, fibroids and early puberty in children.

items.name: Lion’s mane
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; also eaten as food
items.summary: An edible mushroom (Hericium erinaceus) taken for memory, focus and mood; small human trials show mixed results, and most evidence comes from lab and animal studies.

items.name: Liraglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, heart risk and weight
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 medicine, sold as Victoza for type 2 diabetes and Saxenda for weight management, that lowers blood sugar and appetite.

items.name: Low-dose naltrexone (LDN)
items.status_label: Off-label; low-dose forms are compounded
items.summary: Naltrexone, an opioid-blocking addiction drug, taken off-label at much lower doses for chronic pain and inflammatory conditions; small trials have given mixed results.

items.name: MGF
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA Category 3, PEG-MGF under review
items.summary: A lab-made peptide based on a variant of the IGF-1 gene, used for muscle growth and banned in sport; its role in the body is disputed.

items.name: MK-677
items.status_label: FDA Category 2: pharmacies may not compound it
items.summary: An experimental oral drug that mimics the hormone ghrelin to raise growth hormone and IGF-1, taken for muscle, sleep and recovery; FDA bars compounding over heart-failure risk.

items.name: MOTS-c
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding status under FDA review
items.summary: A small peptide encoded in mitochondrial DNA, taken in hopes of improving metabolism, exercise capacity and aging; its effects have only been tested in rodents and cells.

items.name: Magnesium glycinate
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A form of the mineral magnesium bound to the amino acid glycine, taken mainly for sleep and relaxation and to top up magnesium intake.

items.name: Mazdutide
items.status_label: Not approved in the US; approved in China in 2025
items.summary: A drug that activates GLP-1 and glucagon receptors, approved in China in 2025 for weight management and type 2 diabetes; it is not approved in the US.

items.name: Melanotan I (afamelanotide)
items.status_label: FDA-approved implant for a rare light disorder (EPP)
items.summary: A lab-made analog of the skin-darkening hormone alpha-MSH, approved as an implant for a rare light-sensitivity disorder; unlicensed Melanotan I products are used for tanning.

items.name: Melanotan II
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding review pending
items.summary: An unapproved lab-made hormone analog injected for tanning and sometimes for sexual arousal, linked in case reports to mole changes and serious side effects.

items.name: Melatonin
items.status_label: Dietary supplement in the US; prescription elsewhere
items.summary: A hormone the brain makes in the dark to time sleep, sold in the US as a supplement mainly to fall asleep faster or ease jet lag.

items.name: Metformin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes; aging use off-label
items.summary: A prescription pill that lowers blood sugar in type 2 diabetes; some people take it off-label hoping to slow aging, which is unproven.

items.name: Methylene blue
items.status_label: FDA-approved injection for methemoglobinemia only
items.summary: A blue dye and approved hospital drug for a rare blood disorder, now promoted for focus and energy; human evidence for those uses is thin.

items.name: Minoxidil
items.status_label: Topical OTC for hair loss; tablets Rx for blood pressure
items.summary: Minoxidil is an over-the-counter scalp treatment for hereditary hair loss and a prescription tablet for severe high blood pressure; low-dose tablets are used off-label for hair.

items.name: Modafinil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for sleep disorders; Schedule IV
items.summary: A prescription wakefulness drug for narcolepsy, sleep apnea and shift work sleepiness, used off-label for focus; in rested healthy people its effects are small.

items.name: NAC (N-acetylcysteine)
items.status_label: Approved drug; supplement sales tolerated by FDA
items.summary: A modified form of the amino acid cysteine, approved as an antidote for acetaminophen overdose and as a mucus thinner, and sold for decades as a dietary supplement.

items.name: NAD+
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; pharmacies may compound it
items.summary: A molecule cells use to make energy, given by IV drip or injection or taken by mouth by people hoping for more energy and slower aging; human evidence is minimal.

items.name: NMN
items.status_label: Dietary supplement since FDA's September 2025 reversal
items.summary: Nicotinamide mononucleotide, a building block the body uses to make NAD+, taken in hopes of slowing aging and boosting metabolism; human benefits are unproven.

items.name: NR (nicotinamide riboside)
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; GRAS notice for some foods
items.summary: A form of vitamin B3 that raises NAD+, a molecule cells use for energy, taken in hopes of healthier aging; trials show few clear health effects.

items.name: Omega-3 fish oil
items.status_label: Supplement; prescription forms FDA-approved
items.summary: Oils from fish, krill or algae that supply the omega-3 fats EPA and DHA, taken mainly for heart health and to lower triglycerides.

items.name: Orforglipron
items.status_label: FDA-approved for weight management (April 2026)
items.summary: A GLP-1 medicine taken as a pill, sold as Foundayo, approved in April 2026 for weight management in adults with obesity or overweight with a related health problem.

items.name: Ovagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A short synthetic peptide from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for the liver and digestive tract; its exact identity and any benefit in people are poorly documented.

items.name: Oxytocin
items.status_label: FDA-approved injection for labor and delivery
items.summary: A hormone that triggers uterine contractions, approved as an injection to start or strengthen labor; nasal sprays used for mood or social bonding have little supporting evidence.

items.name: PEG-MGF
items.status_label: Not approved; not eligible for pharmacy compounding
items.summary: A lab-made, pegylated version of a short peptide from the IGF-1 gene, promoted for muscle growth and repair but never studied in people.

items.name: PT-141
items.status_label: Approved (Vyleesi) for low desire in premenopausal women
items.summary: A lab-made peptide that activates melanocortin receptors, FDA-approved as Vyleesi for low sexual desire in premenopausal women and also used off-label for libido and erections.

items.name: Pancragen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A four-amino-acid peptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Trp) from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for pancreas function and blood sugar; tested in cells, monkeys and small human studies.

items.name: Pemvidutide
items.status_label: Investigational; phase 3 start not confirmed
items.summary: An experimental drug that activates glucagon and GLP-1 receptors, tested for weight loss and now mainly for fatty-liver disease (MASH) and alcohol use disorder; not FDA-approved.

items.name: Pentadeca Arginate
items.status_label: Not approved; not on any FDA compounding list
items.summary: A peptide described as an arginine salt of the experimental peptide BPC-157, used for injury healing; it has not been tested in published studies and is not FDA-approved.

items.name: Phentermine
items.status_label: FDA-approved for short-term weight loss; Schedule IV
items.summary: A prescription appetite suppressant related to amphetamine, approved for short-term use alongside a weight-loss program; a Schedule IV controlled substance.

items.name: Pramlintide
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Symlin); reported discontinued in the US
items.summary: A lab-made form of the hormone amylin, approved as Symlin for adults with type 1 or type 2 diabetes who use mealtime insulin; reported discontinued in the US.

items.name: Pregnenolone
items.status_label: Supplement; FDA reviewing it for compounding
items.summary: A steroid the body turns into other hormones and brain-active neurosteroids, sold as a supplement and studied in small trials for pain, schizophrenia and bipolar depression.

items.name: Probiotics
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: Live microorganisms such as Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium and Saccharomyces boulardii, taken mainly to prevent antibiotic-related diarrhea and ease gut symptoms.

items.name: Progesterone (micronized)
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription hormone (Prometrium)
items.summary: A prescription form of the natural hormone progesterone, used mainly to protect the uterine lining in postmenopausal women taking estrogen and to treat periods that have stopped.

items.name: Prostamax
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A short lab-made peptide (Lys-Glu-Asp-Pro) from Russian 'bioregulator' research, promoted for prostate health; published evidence is limited to lab studies on cells and DNA.

items.name: Raloxifene
items.status_label: FDA-approved for women after menopause; not for men
items.summary: A prescription SERM pill that lowers the risk of spine fractures and of breast cancer in women after menopause; its label says it is not recommended for men.

items.name: Rapamycin
items.status_label: FDA-approved transplant and LAM drug; not for aging
items.summary: An immune-suppressing transplant drug (sirolimus) that extends lifespan in mice and is being studied in people as a possible way to slow aging.

items.name: Retatrutide
items.status_label: Investigational; not approved, not legal to compound
items.summary: An experimental Eli Lilly drug that activates three hormone receptors (GIP, GLP-1 and glucagon); it is in late-stage obesity trials and is not FDA-approved.

items.name: Rhodiola rosea
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A cold-climate herb (golden root) taken to fight fatigue and stress and lift mood; trials are small and conflicting, and NIH says the evidence is insufficient.

items.name: SLU-PP-332
items.status_label: Not approved; experimental, animal studies only
items.summary: An experimental compound that switches on estrogen-related receptors (ERRs) and mimics some effects of exercise in mice; no human studies have been published.

items.name: SNAP-8 (acetyl octapeptide-3)
items.status_label: Cosmetic ingredient; not an approved drug
items.summary: A lab-made eight-amino-acid peptide used in anti-wrinkle skin products, marketed as a topical alternative to Botox for expression lines.

items.name: SS-31
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Forzinity) for Barth syndrome only
items.summary: A lab-made peptide that targets mitochondria, FDA-approved in 2025 as Forzinity for Barth syndrome and taken off-label for aging and energy based mostly on animal studies.

items.name: Selank
items.status_label: Not approved; not eligible for compounding
items.summary: A lab-made seven-amino-acid peptide based on tuftsin, an immune protein fragment, taken for anxiety and focus; human evidence is one small Russian study.

items.name: Semaglutide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for diabetes, weight, heart, kidney, MASH
items.summary: A prescription GLP-1 medicine, sold as Ozempic, Rybelsus and Wegovy, used to lower blood sugar in type 2 diabetes and to lose weight.

items.name: Semax
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; compounding decision pending
items.summary: A lab-made peptide based on a fragment of the hormone ACTH, registered in Russia as nasal drops and taken for focus, memory and stroke recovery.

items.name: Sermorelin
items.status_label: Compounded by prescription; former approved drug
items.summary: A shortened copy of the brain hormone that tells the pituitary to release growth hormone; once an approved drug, now compounded and used to raise growth hormone and IGF-1.

items.name: Sildenafil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for erectile dysfunction
items.summary: A prescription PDE5-inhibitor pill for erectile dysfunction (Viagra); the same drug is also sold as Revatio for pulmonary arterial hypertension.

items.name: Somatropin (HGH)
items.status_label: FDA-approved; illegal to distribute for anti-aging
items.summary: Lab-made human growth hormone, prescribed for growth hormone deficiency and certain growth disorders; distributing it for anti-aging or bodybuilding is a federal crime.

items.name: Spironolactone
items.status_label: FDA-approved for heart and fluid problems; acne off-label
items.summary: A prescription water pill for heart failure and high blood pressure that also blocks male hormones, so it is used off-label for acne and hair loss in women.

items.name: Survodutide
items.status_label: Investigational; not approved
items.summary: An experimental Boehringer Ingelheim drug that activates glucagon and GLP-1 receptors, in phase 3 trials for obesity and fatty-liver disease; it is not FDA-approved.

items.name: TB-500
items.status_label: Not approved; compounding not yet allowed
items.summary: A synthetic 7-amino-acid fragment of thymosin beta-4, promoted for injury and wound recovery; FDA found no studies of it in people.

items.name: Tadalafil
items.status_label: FDA-approved for ED and enlarged-prostate symptoms
items.summary: A prescription PDE5-inhibitor pill for erectile dysfunction and for urinary symptoms of an enlarged prostate; in trials, its effect on erections lasted up to 36 hours.

items.name: Tamoxifen
items.status_label: FDA-approved for breast cancer; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription SERM that treats hormone-sensitive breast cancer, including in men, and lowers breast cancer risk in high-risk women; it is also used off-label for male breast enlargement and infertility.

items.name: Taurine
items.status_label: Dietary supplement; common energy-drink ingredient
items.summary: An amino acid found in energy drinks and supplements, taken for energy and healthy aging; lifespan gains seen in animals haven't been shown in people.

items.name: Telmisartan
items.status_label: FDA-approved for high blood pressure; aging off-label
items.summary: A prescription blood pressure and heart-protection drug; in lab studies it also partly activates a metabolic switch (PPAR-gamma), but benefits for healthy aging are unproven.

items.name: Tesamorelin
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Egrifta) for HIV-related belly fat
items.summary: An FDA-approved, lab-made version of the brain hormone that triggers growth hormone release, used to shrink excess deep belly fat in adults with HIV.

items.name: Testagen
items.status_label: Not FDA-approved; not on FDA compounding lists
items.summary: A Russian dietary-supplement peptide from Khavinson's 'bioregulator' research, promoted for male reproductive health and testosterone; human evidence is one small study by its developers.

items.name: Testosterone
items.status_label: FDA-approved for male hypogonadism; Schedule III
items.summary: A male sex hormone (androgen) prescribed to men with low testosterone from testicular, pituitary or hypothalamic problems; a Schedule III controlled substance in the US.

items.name: Thymosin alpha-1
items.status_label: Not approved; FDA advisers voted against compounding
items.summary: A 28-amino-acid immune-signaling peptide, sold abroad as Zadaxin mainly for hepatitis B and taken for immune support; FDA found the evidence insufficient for every use it reviewed.

items.name: Thymosin beta-4
items.status_label: Not approved; eye drops in phase 3 trials
items.summary: A natural 43-amino-acid protein promoted for injury recovery based on animal studies; tested in people as eye drops and a skin gel with mixed results, it is not approved and differs from TB-500.

items.name: Tirzepatide
items.status_label: FDA-approved for type 2 diabetes, weight and sleep apnea
items.summary: A prescription injection, sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound, that activates two hormone receptors (GIP and GLP-1) to lower blood sugar and body weight.

items.name: Tongkat ali
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: Root extract of the Southeast Asian shrubby tree Eurycoma longifolia, long used as an aphrodisiac and taken mainly to raise testosterone; evidence comes from a few small trials.

items.name: Tretinoin
items.status_label: FDA-approved for acne; one cream for fine wrinkles
items.summary: A prescription skin medicine for acne; one cream version is also approved to soften fine wrinkles, blotchy pigment and roughness of facial skin.

items.name: Triptorelin
items.status_label: FDA-approved (Trelstar, Triptodur)
items.summary: A prescription hormone drug that, with continued use, shuts down testosterone and estrogen production; approved for advanced prostate cancer and for early puberty in children.

items.name: Turkesterone
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: A plant steroid from Ajuga turkestanica, promoted for building muscle; the few small human studies found no effect, and products often contain less than labeled.

items.name: Vitamin B12
items.status_label: Supplement; injections and nasal gel by prescription
items.summary: An essential vitamin for nerves, red blood cells and DNA, taken to prevent or treat deficiency, which is more likely with age, vegan diets and some medicines.

items.name: Vitamin D3
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: The form of vitamin D the skin makes in sunlight, taken to keep bones healthy and to correct or prevent low vitamin D levels.

items.name: Zinc
items.status_label: Dietary supplement
items.summary: An essential mineral needed for immune function, wound healing and hundreds of enzymes, taken mostly to shorten colds and support immunity.

items.name: hCG
items.status_label: FDA-approved prescription biologic; not for weight loss
items.summary: A pregnancy hormone that acts like LH, prescribed to stimulate the testes in men with pituitary-related hypogonadism, to treat undescended testes in boys and to trigger ovulation.

items.name: hMG
items.status_label: FDA-approved biologic for IVF; off-label in men
items.summary: A prescription fertility injection of FSH and LH activity purified from postmenopausal women's urine, approved for IVF; it is used off-label in men to start sperm production.
